s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: Painful bruise on the hand that persisted despite icing and resting
Ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
Heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on Magnetic Resonance Imaging
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The patient sustained a twisting injury to the affected hand while participating in acroyoga 2 years prior
The bruise and pain initially appeared a few days after the injury
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but was otherwise unremarkable
Magnetic Resonance Imaging showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

shortlist.label: Hemosiderotic fibrohistiocytic lipomatous lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition

shortlist.label: Nora lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by a painful subcutaneous mass with histological features of spindle cells and fat globules, matching the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Spindle cell lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Shows similar histological features to the patient's lesion, including spindled cells and fat globules

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Has overlapping histological features with the patient's lesion, including spindled cells and fat globules

shortlist.label: Angiolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered given the patient's presentation of a painful subcutaneous mass, although less likely than other options

raw.rationale: The presence of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, along with lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, and immunohistochemistry strongly positive for CD34, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Nora lesion
rejected.why: Nora lesion typically presents as a painful, subcutaneous mass, but the pathology and immunohistochemistry results do not match

rejected.label: Spindle cell lipoma
rejected.why: Spindle cell lipoma typically lacks the extensive pigment deposition seen in this case

rejected.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
rejected.why: Pleomorphic lipoma typically has a different immunohistochemical profile and lacks the hemosiderotic component

rejected.label: Angiolipoma
rejected.why: Angiolipoma typically has a prominent vascular component, which is not described in this case
